title: Tech Note: Optimizing Windows NT for High-Performance with 4D Server
author: Christopher Chapman
featured_technology: Windows NT pagefile / virtual memory tuning
Windows NT display and desktop configuration

historical_commentary.text: This note gives concrete Windows NT tuning recommendations for 4D Server — using NTFS, sizing the pagefile relative to RAM and spreading it across drives, compressing the data file's directory, launching 4DSERVER.EXE with REALTIME process priority via a batch file, and minimizing display/desktop overhead — all aimed at maximizing server throughput on 1996-era hardware; while the specific numeric formulas and OS-version details (Windows NT Workstation/Server, MB-scale RAM) are entirely obsolete relative to modern hardware and OS memory management, the general principles of using a fast filesystem, giving a database server process high scheduling priority, and minimizing unnecessary desktop/display overhead remain conceptually recognizable server-tuning ideas.
related_updates: Modern Windows Server versions and 4D Server run on vastly more capable hardware with automatic, far more sophisticated virtual memory and I/O management, making these manual 1996-era pagefile-sizing formulas obsolete
NTFS has been the default/standard Windows filesystem for decades; the note's advocacy for NTFS over FAT/HPFS is no longer a meaningful choice
REALTIME process priority tuning via a manual batch file is largely superseded by modern OS process/service management and 4D Server's own updated deployment guidance
